scope: Theorem 6.4 (Uniform propagation of finite packet arrays) of the manuscript “Elliptic capacity propagation and Fourier restriction to the sphere” (preprints/Elliptic-capacity-propagation-and-Fourier-restriction-to-the-sphere-September-24-2026/Elliptic-capacity-propagation-and-Fourier-restriction-to-the-sphere-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 077 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 669efdbef9150144), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 71. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 0 < κ < 1/10, the continued phase, a bounded frequency region, and the window system above. For every fixed admissible complexity range and every ε > 0, there is a finite constant C such that A(Tmd)3 ≤ Cm10κ+ε G(d)3 (6.8) for every finite complex initial array d and every terminal coordinate mask in that range. The same estimate holds with A(d)3 on the right. The constant is uniform in m, N, d, and the masks; it may depend on κ, ε, the complexity range, the fixed phase and frequency region, and the windows. Equivalently, γ ≤ 10κ. (6.9)
